item.title: Trump releases plan to rebuild US shipbuilding industry
item.description: The Trump administration has released a Maritime Action Plan to rebuild the U.S. shipbuilding and maritime industries, funded in part by port fees on cargo delivered to the U.S. on ships made in China, which were paused for one year. Sen. Todd Young of Indiana said, "It’s time to make American ships again.”

item.title: Indianapolis investigators seek public’s help in restaurant fire probe
item.description: Indianapolis fire investigators are seeking information and camera footage from the public following a restaurant fire early Wednesday morning on the city's south side. Hot Pot Lovers sustained heavy damage. The fire also caused smoke damage to a nearby grocery store.

item.title: IMPD makes arrest after man’s fatal overdose
item.description: Kameron Tinnins was arrested for his role in a fatal overdose that occurred in September, after police found evidence tied to the overdose during a search of his apartment.

item.title: Homeland Security shutdown: What you need to know
item.description: The U.S. Department of Homeland Security is facing a partial government shutdown due to Congress not funding the agency, but most workers will remain on the job, and the public likely won't notice much of a change.

item.title: Indiana ‘deadline’ approaches for possible Chicago Bears stadium deal
item.description: Indiana leaders are pushing for a financial agreement for a potential Chicago Bears stadium in northwest Indiana to be finalized before the end of the legislative session on Feb. 27, 2026.

item.title: Comedian Mike Epps gives teens a path forward through new boxing gym
item.description: Comedian Mike Epps opened a boxing gym in Indianapolis to give teens a safe haven to build confidence and learn conflict resolution.

item.title: IMPD arrests 6 at Lugar Plaza, a space ‘meant to be safe, welcoming’
item.description: Six people were arrested at Lugar Plaza in downtown Indianapolis on Feb. 13, 2026, for narcotics-related offenses and outstanding warrants, following four other arrests earlier this week. Indianapolis police want to maintain a safe environment for the community.

item.title: IMPD chief condemns officer’s language in viral traffic stop video
item.description: The Indianapolis Metropolitan Police Department's new chief defended a Feb. 6 traffic stop in which an officer threatened to kill a teenage driver, while condemning the language used by the officer. Findings from an internal review of the traffic stop have been given to the Marion County Prosecutor’s Office for consideration.

item.title: Plans for ICE office in Carmel spark fear and uncertainty
item.description: The Carmel City Council president has confirmed that U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement will establish an office in Carmel. The plan has caused fear and concern among community members, some of whom have coworkers, friends and family members affected by ICE's actions.
